title: Why Company Loyalty Costs You 50% in Lifetime Earnings
hook_text: STAYING AT ONE COMPANY COSTS YOU 50%

beats.say: Staying at the same company for more than two years costs you an average of 50 percent in lifetime earnings.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a weathered metal desk key resting on dark, rain-slicked asphalt under cold sodium light.

beats.say: You clock in early. You skip lunch. You wait for that annual review.
beats.visual: Low angle silhouette of a single office tower edge cutting into a heavy gray fog at blue hour.

beats.say: So why does your paycheck barely move while your workload doubles?
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of an empty highway at night cut by the harsh headlights of a distant truck.

beats.say: Most people assume internal raises reward hard work and dedication over time.
beats.visual: High angle shot of wet concrete stairs descending into a dark, empty underground subway station.

beats.say: The math proves otherwise. Internal salary raises average just 3 percent a year.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a brass door handle reflecting a cold fluorescent tube in an empty hallway.

beats.say: Meanwhile, job-switching yields 10 to 20 percent increases due to market-rate anchoring.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a single amber streetlamp casting long shadows across an abandoned gravel parking lot.

beats.say: How much does staying put actually drain from your career bank account?
beats.visual: Low angle view of a rusted fire escape ladder climbing a damp brick wall under overcast skies.

beats.say: Every year you stay without a major title jump, your skills get underpriced by the open market.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of heavy iron chains resting on cold concrete under single practical light.

beats.say: Companies budget more for new hires than they do for loyal veterans.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of open water at dusk under a flat, heavy gray horizon.

beats.say: The market pays for what you can do right now elsewhere, not where you started.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a lone human figure walking along a stark ridge line against a fading evening sky.

beats.say: Test your worth on the open market every two years to capture your true price.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a massive concrete bridge support looming against a dark, starless night sky.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a brass mechanical lock turning sharply in deep shadow under blue hour light.

caption: Company loyalty is a quiet tax on your earning potential. Time to look at the numbers. #CareerAdvice #PersonalFinance #MoneyTok #SalaryNegotiation #WealthBuilding
description: Internal salary raises average only 3 percent, while job-switching yields 10 to 20 percent increases due to market-rate anchoring. Staying too long costs you lifetime earnings.
first_comment: When was the last time you tested your market value?

facts.basis: Industry standard benchmark data on annual internal merit increases versus external hiring budgets.

facts.basis: Federal Reserve and labor market data comparing job hopper wage growth to static retention raises.
